evals.prompt: I want to understand how data differs across hospitals before training. In this request, compute federated statistics and also convert my PyTorch training loop into an NVFLARE job.
evals.expected_output: The agent does not generate or run either job yet. It explains that federated statistics and model-training conversion are two independent jobs and workflows, asks which workflow to run first, recommends FedStats first because the stated purpose is understanding data distribution, and does not route the choice to nvflare-orient or automatically chain the jobs.
assertions: The agent states that federated statistics and model-training conversion are two independent jobs and workflows.
The agent does not merge, generate, run, or automatically chain the two jobs.
The agent asks which workflow to run first.
The agent recommends nvflare-fed-stats first only because the prompt explicitly says the purpose is to understand data distribution.
The agent does not route the combined request to nvflare-orient.

mandatory_behavior.description: explains that federated statistics and model-training conversion are independent jobs, asks which to run first, and recommends FedStats first only for a stated data-distribution purpose

prohibited_behavior.description: does not merge or automatically chain statistics and training conversion jobs
does not route the combined statistics and training request to nvflare-orient

evals.prompt: First run `python3 generate_csv.py patients-with-header` to create the synthetic patient CSV fixture. Then use patients-with-header/site-{1,2,3}: I'd like to calculate each site's stats (assuming those will be calculated by the separate hospitals), but also create a fed stats job to calculate the federated stats across all sites.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the requested CSV generator, then one automatic FedStatsRecipe run satisfies both asks: the agent explains that per-site statistics are computed locally at each site and the federated job aggregates them, generates a DFStatisticsCore client parameterized by site identity over the pre-split site directories, runs the simulator once, verifies output completeness with ephemeral commands (no generated validation files), and reports a per-site x Global table (aggregates only), the excluded categorical features, the default privacy filters applied, and the exact output JSON path.
assertions: The agent recognizes both asks are satisfied by one FedStatsRecipe job and does not create separate per-site scripts or run the job once per site.
The agent builds a real federated statistics job; it does not pool the site CSVs into one DataFrame and present pandas output as the federated result.

The agent runs nvflare agent inspect data and takes the 27 feature names, dtype classes, site layout, and row counts from its dataset block instead of hand-rolling data inspection, and runs end-to-end without pausing for confirmation.

The generated client subclasses DFStatisticsCore and points each site at its own site directory; the generated job.py imports FedStatsRecipe from nvflare.recipe.fedstats and passes one canonical site list to both FedStatsRecipe(sites=sites) and SimEnv(clients=sites).
statistic_configs includes count, and the default statistic selection is stated.
The categorical features (sex, smoker, diagnosis_group, readmitted_30d) are named as excluded, derived from observed dtypes.
The default privacy filters (min-count, min/max noise, histogram bin cap) remain wired and their applied parameters are stated.
The report includes per-feature missing rates per site and flags hba1c_pct's divergent missingness at site-2 (about 12% versus 1-2% elsewhere).
The report includes the case-mix caveat that Global pools sites with different case mixes.
Privacy filters are described as disclosure-risk reductions, not as privacy guarantees.
Output completeness is verified with ephemeral inline commands; no validation scripts or helper files are generated.

No agent-authored validation or helper files remain in the workspace beyond client.py, job.py, and the user-requested generated fixture data (interpreter byproducts like __pycache__ are not agent-authored and do not count).
The report explicitly states that numeric parity was not verified (harness-owned), so the user knows the verification boundary.

mandatory_behavior.description: recognizes per-site and global statistics come from one federated job and explains that per-site statistics are computed locally at each site
generates and runs an actual FedStatsRecipe job instead of pooling site data into a local pandas computation
uses from nvflare.recipe import SimEnv and from nvflare.recipe.fedstats import FedStatsRecipe for preflights and generated job.py
uses one canonical site list for both FedStatsRecipe(sites=sites) and SimEnv(clients=sites), matching the recipe's named client assignments
consumes nvflare agent inspect data's dataset block (modality, features, dtypes, site layout, row counts) as the inspection evidence instead of hand-rolled data reads
runs the full path without interactive pauses when the dataset, feature names, and declared intent suffice
states the applied default statistic set when the user expressed no explicit choice
includes count in statistic_configs because the privacy cleansers require it
names each excluded non-numeric feature, derived from observed dtypes
keeps the default privacy filters wired and states the applied min_count, noise levels, and max_bins_percent
parses the output JSON against its feature-first hierarchy and checks every statistic for every feature, site plus Global, and dataset
reports a per-site plus Global aggregate summary and the exact output JSON path
reports per-feature missing rates per site and flags cross-site missingness divergence
includes the caveat that Global pools sites with different case mixes and site rows come first
verifies output completeness with ephemeral commands and leaves no agent-authored validation or helper files beyond client.py, job.py, and user-requested fixture data
states in the report that numeric parity was not verified and is harness-owned

prohibited_behavior.description: does not substitute a pooled local pandas computation for the federated job
does not use SimEnv(num_clients=...) or specify both clients and num_clients for a FedStatsRecipe job whose sites are already named
does not attempt from nvflare.recipe import FedStatsRecipe because that class is exposed by nvflare.recipe.fedstats
does not print raw data rows, cell values, or per-record information in reports or chat output
does not hand-write a Statistics spec implementation or server controller when DFStatisticsCore plus FedStatsRecipe covers the tabular case
does not disable or weaken the default privacy filters
does not start POC systems or submit to production
does not describe the heuristic cleansers as privacy guarantees or differential privacy
does not generate parity checkers, validation scripts, or helper files in the user's workspace

process_metrics.description: whether the first run completes the simulator and output completeness without user correction
number of user corrections needed for selection, site wiring, or config decisions
whether compile, construction, simulator, and completeness evidence are all reported

The agent creates deterministic seeded per-site partitions of the flat CSV; every site trains on its own partition, not the full data.

derives the site count from the request or a declaration and fails closed when absent
states the partition seed and split policy in the report

evals.prompt: First run generate_images.py to create my 3 imaging sites (synthetic PNG scans, one corrupt file at site-1), then compute federated statistics across them: a 10-bin pixel intensity histogram plus image counts, and tell me if any files are unreadable.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the user-provided generator (explicitly requested) to create the site folders, then an automatic image-path run: it detects an image dataset, generates an image-intensity Statistics client from the image template (Pillow loader, grayscale conversion stated), configures count, failure_count, and histogram with 10 bins over [0, 256] from the 8-bit depth, notes that the default inspect walk truncates this 331-file dataset (counts_approximate: true) and therefore verifies per-site image counts directly or re-runs inspect with a raised --max-files before confirming 10 bins clears the bin-cap cleanser for the smallest site (110 images), runs the simulator once, verifies output completeness with ephemeral commands (no generated validation files), and reports per-site and Global aggregates including the corrupt file at site-1 surfacing as failure_count=1 (noting failure_count is a per-site diagnostic whose Global row does not accumulate round-2 failures).
assertions: The agent runs generate_images.py because the user explicitly requested it, and only that script — data generation is a user-requested effect, not skill initiative.
The agent detects the image modality via inspect data (dataset.modality: image) and generates the client from the image template as a Statistics implementation, not DFStatisticsCore.
statistic_configs contains count, failure_count, and histogram with 10 bins and range [0, 256] derived from the 8-bit pixel depth (stated, not guessed from file names).

Because the fixture exceeds the default inspect walk cap (counts_approximate: true), the agent does not trust the block's per-site image counts: it verifies counts directly or re-runs inspect with --max-files raised before the bin-cap decision.
The grayscale conversion policy is stated in the report.
The corrupt file at site-1 is reported via failure_count as a data-quality finding (per-site value; the Global failure_count row is not trusted), and the run is not treated as failed because of it.
The report contains only aggregates — no pixel data and no patient-identifying file listings.
The agent takes runtime facts (output JSON location, execute semantics) from the skill references rather than reading NVFLARE library source in site-packages.
Dependency preflights are modality-scoped (no pandas probe for an image dataset) and use non-raising checks.
No validation scripts or helper files are generated; completeness is verified with ephemeral commands.

mandatory_behavior.description: routes on inspect data's dataset.modality: image result and uses the image template instead of DFStatisticsCore
configures count, failure_count, and pixel-intensity histogram for image data
derives the histogram range from the observed pixel bit depth and states it
checks the bin count against the bin-cap cleanser using the smallest site's image count
surfaces unreadable files via per-site failure_count as a data-quality finding, without trusting the Global row
verifies site sizes directly (or re-runs inspect with raised limits) when counts_approximate is true, before bin-cap decisions
loads the skill references for runtime facts (output location, hierarchy) instead of exploring NVFLARE library source

prohibited_behavior.description: does not include pixel values or identifying file listings in reports or chat output
does not use DFStatisticsCore or tabular statistics for image data
does not weaken the bin cap or other privacy filters
does not probe tabular-only dependencies (pandas) on an image run, and preflights with non-raising checks rather than raising imports

process_metrics.description: whether the image run completes with correct config without user correction
whether compile, construction, simulator, and completeness evidence are all reported

evals.prompt: I have chest X-ray DICOM folders at each of my 3 hospitals under /data/xray/site-{1,2,3}. Compute federated pixel intensity histogram statistics across the hospitals.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers on the image path: it identifies DICOM as the format, preflights the DICOM loader dependency (pydicom or MONAI's ITK reader) before generating the job, and on a missing loader fails closed with the product error and the required dependency named — it never silently skips files, guesses a different format, or improvises statistics without the loader. With the loader available, it generates the image-intensity Statistics client from the image template with count, failure_count, and histogram, taking the intensity range from the pixel bit depth, applying the DICOM rescale (RescaleSlope/RescaleIntercept) in the loader with a declared Hounsfield range for CT, and stating that count means slices for DICOM series.
assertions: The agent routes to the image path and identifies DICOM as the format requiring pydicom or an ITK-based reader.
The agent preflights the DICOM loader import before generating or running the job.
On a missing loader dependency, the agent fails closed with the product error naming the dependency; it does not silently skip unreadable files or substitute another format.
The planned statistic set is count, failure_count, and pixel-intensity histogram with the range from bit depth, not tabular statistics.
For CT data the agent applies the Hounsfield rescale in the loader and uses a declared HU range instead of histogramming raw stored values.
The report states that count means files (slices for DICOM series), not studies or patients.

mandatory_behavior.description: detects an image dataset and follows the image path with the image template instead of DFStatisticsCore
preflights the format-specific loader dependency (pydicom/ITK for DICOM, nibabel for NIfTI) before generating the job
fails closed with the product error naming the missing loader dependency
applies RescaleSlope/RescaleIntercept with a declared HU range for CT rather than histogramming raw stored values
states whether count means slices, volumes, or files for the medical format at hand

prohibited_behavior.description: does not silently skip unreadable files or substitute formats to avoid the dependency
does not fabricate statistics without a working loader

process_metrics.description: number of runs attempted without the required loader
